tossups.text: One holder of this position came out of retirement to threaten Ayatollah Khomeini and was at the center of the BCCI scandal. Besides Clark Clifford and Melvin Laird, another occupant of this post sent a controversial memorandum on the sentencing of Jonathan Pollard and was nicknamed "the Knife," while its first holder championed a major legislation in 1947 but later leaped to his death from a room at Bethesda Naval Hospital. For 10 points, name this cabinet position of Caspar Weinberger and James Forrestal, held under Kennedy by Robert McNamara, which partially replaced the Secretary of War.

One collection by this name is housed in the Pallazzo Venier dei Leoni in Venice. Its newest branch opened in Las Vegas's Venetian resort in 2001, while the original was contracted by Hilla Rebay as the Museum of Non-Objective Painting. The inverted ziggurat and the winding spiral connecting the galleries were designed by Frank Lloyd Wright. For 10 points, name these museums, whose flagship branch houses the world's largest Kandinsky collection, in Manhattan.

A character in this novel throws a child out of a crowd of farm workers after shouting at an armed group of soldiers to "Take the extra minute and stick it up [their] *** ["bleep"]." Another character in this novel states that a priest "found the fourth state of matter" in Latin when he sees the priest levitating. An orphaned girl in this novel eats only dirt and whitewash when she is young. A man in this novel is tied to a chestnut tree after going insane and only speaking in Latin. That character, the patriarch of this novel's family, meets the gypsy Melquiades and takes his son to see ice. This novel ends with a whirlwind destroying a house, and begins with Aureliano standing in front of a firing squad. For 10 points, name this novel about the Buendía family by Gabriel García Márquez.

Tippu Tip established a slave trading station at Tabora in this nation. This nation's scenic Stone Town was once part of the Sultanate of Oman and is located on an eastern archipelago. Some rare black rhinos live in the N-gorong-oro Crater in this country's north. This home of Mount Meru has a national park around the Olduvai Gorge. This nation contains Mount Kilimanjaro and Serengeti National Park. For 10 points, name this nation with a former capital at Dar es Salaam, formed by the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar.

When passing through turbid materials, this particle can retain linear motion and is said to be "ballistic." In a system with two of these particles, mass can be created at high energies since these particle can become a fermion-antifermion pair. This massless particle has an energy inversely proportional to its wavelength. These particles are bombarded at a metal and electrons are emitted in an effect explained by Einstein. For 10 points, name this particle that exhibits wave-like behavior and is the basic unit of all electromagnetic radiation, including light.

He first gained notoriety for the True Born Englishman in 1701 and was jailed during the reign of Queen Anne for publishing the satirical Shortest Way with the Dissenters. One work by this author tells the story of an adulterous, incestuous female thief and con artist, while another work was partially based upon a man exiled due to his involvement in the Monmouth Rebellion that follows the story of the shipwrecked sailor, Alexander Selkirk. For 10 points, identify this author of Moll Flanders and Robinson Crusoe.

This non-European country's ancient artwork includes sculptures that are decorated with powdered quartz over a vitreous substance called "faience." A motif of this country's ancient art features names enclosed within an oval and a single horizontal line, called a cartouche. This country's funereal art includes small sculptures called ushabti, in which subjects were depicted with their arms folded across their chests. An artwork from this country called the "Younger Memnon" depicts its subject wearing the uraeus, a cobra symbol on top of the crown. A bust of one of its female rulers was found at Amarna in 1912. Statues at Abu Simbel can be found in, for 10 points, what country whose art includes sarcophagi that have hieroglyphics inscribed on their covers?

During one of these events, Sergei Pankejeff saw a tree full of wolves. After studying one of these titled "Irma's Injection", the concepts of "wish fulfillment" and the "royal road to the unconscious" were developed by Sigmund Freud in his "Interpretation of" these events. Usually occurring during the REM stage, for 10 points, name these series of thoughts and images that occur during sleep.

In human physiology, this structure is essential for spleen functions. It plays a key role in the immune system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this lymph-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The lymph is a key component of the Immune system, involved in spleen functions.

tossups.text: In this play, a talkative character who declares that "brevity is the soul of wit" spies on the protagonist and his mother, and is stabbed through a curtain. A goblet of poisoned wine and a poison-coated sword are prepared for a duel in this play, but end up killing Gertrude and Laertes instead. This play's protagonist tells Ophelia to "get thee to a nunnery" and vows to get revenge on Claudius for his father's death in, for 10 points, what Shakespeare tragedy about the Prince of Denmark?

His Piano Concerto No. 3 was originally intended to be a symphony but was published as a one-movement Allegro brillante posthumously. He wrote an un-numbered Manfred Symphony between his 4th and 5th, and his 7th was left unfinished at his death. The opening 36-bar Andante introduction is marked "sempre marcatissimo" in his Serenade for Strings, and his visit to inspired his Capriccio italien. Using part of La Marseillaise in one piece that often uses canons at the end, this is, for 10 points, what Russian composer of the 1812 Overture and Symphony No. 6, Pathetique?

Osbert of Clare wrote a biography of this ruler, whose chief advisor was Robert of Jumieges. This ruler put down rioters in Dover who resisted his brother-in-law Eustace of Boulogne, and he seized the property of his mother Emma after coming to power. He sent an expedition under Siward the Fat to punish the Scottish king Macbeth for harboring exiles loyal to the father of his wife Edith, Godwin. The builder of Westminster Abbey, he took the throne after the death of his half-brother Harthecanute. For 10 points, identify this son of Aethelred the Unready and last ruler of the House of Wessex, a famously pious King of England who was canonized in 1161.
acceptableAnswers: but do not accept any numbers

tossups.text: In human physiology, this structure is essential for arteries vs veins vs capillaries. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this aorta-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The aorta is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in arteries vs veins vs capillaries.

tossups.text: In the film Synecdoche, New York, Caden receives a MacArthur fellowship after directing this play, and in a 2016 Asghar Farhadi film this play is performed by the central couple in Tehran. A character in this play states "Nothing's planted. I haven't got a thing in the ground" while obsessing over the garden in his backyard during a meal at Frank's Chop House. Stage directions in this play call for a flute to play in any scene where nostalgia is evoked. The title character's father had found success in the Alaskan wilderness while his brother Ben had made a fortune in Africa, both of which are contrasted with the main character's unsuccessful life in Brooklyn. Featuring the characters Biff, Happy, and Willy, for 10 points, name this play about the Loman family, a work by Arthur Miller.

In this state, a thin layer of melting ice allows some stones to "sail" across the surface of Racetrack Playa. A national park in this state contains the Bridalveil Fall vista and was advocated for by John Muir's (myurzz) Sierra Club. In that national park in this state, Glacier Point gives views of El Capitan and Half Dome. For 10 points, name this state which contains Death Valley and Yosemite (yoh-SEM-ih-tee).

He wrote about the American hotel industry in his Work of Art, while a young actress is the subject of his novel Bethel Merriday. Many of his readers were shocked by the sexual frankness of Cass Timberlane, while others were shocked by his novel about a man who discovers that he has African-American blood, Kingsblood Royal. He wrote about a retired automobile tycoon and his wife in his novel Dodsworth, and imagined a fascist takeover of the United States in It Can't Happen Here. For 10 points, name this American author who wrote about a physician, minister, and realtor in Arrowsmith, Elmer Gantry, and Babbit.

A palace in this country contains four sunken gardens and the Pavilion of the Fifty, as well as the Pavilion of the Heliotrope. Walls in one city in this country were allegedly painted one color to ward off flies; that "blue city" is Chefchaouen. This country contained places called "saline areas," which were Jewish quarters called mellahs. This country is the westernmost country to feature citadels called kasbahs and contains the El Badi Palace, which was constructed after this country's forces defeated the Portuguese at the Battle of the Three Kings. This country's forces defeated the Songhai at Tondibi during the rule of Ahmad al-Mansur. This country's Maghreb-style architecture was influenced by the Saadi and Almoravid Dynasties. For 10 points, name this North African country, whose four Imperial Cities include Fez and Casablanca.

This organ receives lactate as part of the Cori cycle and converts it to glucose. This organ receives deoxygenated blood from the spleen via the portal vein. This organ contains Kupffer cells, and its failure to break down bilirubin can cause jaundice. This organ is inflamed in hepatitis and is damaged in cirrhosis, which can result from alcohol overconsumption. For ten points, name this largest internal organ of the human body.

The double dividends hypothesis pertains to the effects of this concept, of which the Pigouvian type is used to match the individual and societal marginal cost curves. This concept is influenced by marginal benefits received in Lindahl's model. Frank P. Ramsey proposed that, like monopolistic pricing, this should be inversely proportional to the price elasticity of demand in order to reduce deadweight losses. The Laffer curve plots revenue against its rate. Supply-side economics, promoted by Ronald Reagan, includes their reduction. For 10 points, name these levies imposed by a government.

Caesar's dam is part of a tunnel system built to transport water from this mountain range's Karun River. In this range, the Si-o-se-pol is the largest of 11 historical bridges that cross the Zayanderud. This range contains ruins at Hegmataneh near Baba Tahir's mausoleum. Neanderthal fossils were found in the Shanidar, Bisitun, and Wezmeh Caves in this mountain range. The Lurs are an ethnic group in this mountain range, whose highest peak is Qash-Mastan on Mount Dena. A trilingual cuneiform inscription was discovered at this range's Mount Behistun. This mountain range separates cities like Qom and Shiraz from Mesopotamia. For 10 points, name this mountain range south of the Alborz in western Iran.

parts.text: This term refers to the string of uprisings that occurred in many middle eastern states against repressive governments between 2010 and 2012. This revolutionary wave has led to ongoing conflicts in Syria and Libya.

In 2011, military backed protesters managed to remove this autocratic president of Egypt. This president, who had previously ruled for 30 years, was recently acquitted of crimes against protesters in the 2011 uprising.

The revolutions in the Arab Spring mostly failed to bring positive change to the nations where they occurred. Name the only country to have gained a pluralistic, constitutional democratic government from its revolution. This country's revolution was considered the first in the Arab Spring.

bonuses.leadin: For Ten points each, answer some questions about some recent uprisings in the Middle East:

parts.text: Identify this artist whose most notable work is in an Art Nouveau style and shows a couple doing the title action, The Kiss.
Most of The Kiss is this color, including the background and many of the rectangles covering the man's body. This color was also often used in Byzantine mosaics.
This other work by Klimt uses gold rain between the title figure's legs to represent Zeus visiting her. The title character in this work wears a purple veil.

bonuses.leadin: This first president of the Vienna Secession painted several portraits of Adele Bloch-Bauer. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Californian author of The Moon is Down, more famous for works like The Grapes of Wrath and Of Mice and Men.
This Steinbeck novel parallels the story of Cain and Abel with the twins Caleb and Aron, the sons of a man who marries Cathy Ames, Adam Trask.
This series of four stories centers on Jody Tiflin, who lives on a ranch and meets the Mexican Gitano in "The Great Mountains" after Gabilan dies of cold in "The Gift".

bonuses.leadin: In one work, this author wrote about Colonel Lanser's occupation of a town during a war similar to World War II. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This territory is home to Anderson Air Force Base. It is the largest of the Mariana Islands, and its capital is at Hagatna.
The United States gained this territory in 1917 by purchasing it from Denmark. The cities of St. Croix and St. Thomas are located in this archipelago.
This Carribean island territory was devastated by Hurricane Maria in 2017. This territory was gained by the US after the Spanish-American War.

bonuses.leadin: Identify some territories owned by the United States. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this alphabetically second namesake of a doubly-eponymous law that states absorbance equals the product of the molar absorption coefficient, concentration, and path length.
Johann Heinrich Lambert proved that this number is irrational. It is the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter, and it is often approximated as 3.14.
Lambert developed a law concerning the intensity from a diffusely reflecting surface that is named for this trigonometric function. It also names a generalization of the Pythagorean theorem.

bonuses.leadin: This man is the namesake of the CGS unit for luminance. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this man who wrote about the oil empire of James Ross and it's impact on his sun Bunny in the novel Oil!

In this Sinclair work, Jurgis Rudkus moves his family from Lithuania to Chicago, where he is subjected to the horrors of the Packingtown slaughterhouses. It helped lead to the passing of the Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906.
Sinclair wrote 11 novels, including Between Two Worlds and World's End, focusing on this central character.The third installment featuring him, Dragon's Teeth, won the 1943 Pulitzer Prize.

bonuses.leadin: In addition to his fiction, this man came in second in the 1934 California gubernatorial election under the End Poverty in California campaign. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this set of six marches often played at graduations which contains a famous Trio accompanied by the lyrics of "Land of Hope and Glory."
Pomp and Circumstance was composed by this English man whose "Nimrod" section in his Enigma Variations was inspired by Augustus Jaeger.
Edward Elgar also composed this musical piece which is based on a poem by Cardinal Newman. It describes the title man's judgement by God and contains the aria, Sanctus fortis.

bonuses.leadin: Its title originates from Act III of Shakespeare's Othello. For 10 points each:

parts.text: How much would it cost in total if Katrina purchased 104 gift cards worth $20 each?
Katrina finds one store that is willing to give her a 10% discount for buying so many cards. How much would it cost Katrina with the discount?
Katrina ends up buying the cards at full price, but buys 5 less because some people retired. How much total in gift cards did Katrina end up giving out?

bonuses.leadin: COMPUTATION: Katrina wants to buy $20 gift cards for her 104 employees. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with cardiac muscle features.
What is the main function of the sarcomere in the musculoskeletal system?
Name another component of the musculoskeletal system related to cardiac muscle features.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human musculoskeletal system.

parts.text: Name this author of the novels Palace Walk, Palace of Desire, and Sugar Street, winner of the 1988 Nobel Prize in Literature.
Along with Tawfiq el-Hakim and the poet Khalil Gibran, Naguib Mahfouz is one of the primary literary figures in this language.
Mahfouz hails from this country, in which Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra is partially set.

bonuses.leadin: He wrote a saga about the Al-Jawad family and the allegory of Abrahamic religion Children of Gebelawi. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this prolific portrait-painter who also painted Aristotle Contemplating a Bust of Homer and The Night Watch.
This other artist made several paintings of girls reading letters and receiving music lessons, but is best known for Girl with a Pearl Earring.
Rembrandt and Vermeer both came from this country, where their paintings are on display in the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam.

bonuses.leadin: The focused light in this artist's work is sometimes called his "spotlight effect." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this island nation, formerly known as Ceylon. It is located near the southern tip of India.
This organization, founded by Vellupillai Prabhakaran, fought the Sinhalese majority for an ethnic state in Sri Lanka. Its "Black" unit is credited with inventing the suicide vest.
This sixth Prime Minister of India was assassinated by a member of the Tamil Tigers wearing an RTX laden belt. His wife Sonia became the president of the Congress Party after his death.

bonuses.leadin: This ethnic majority on this island nation is the Sinhalese. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with b cells and antibodies.
What is the main function of the T cell in the immune system?
Name another component of the immune system related to b cells and antibodies.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human immune system.

parts.text: Name this short story set on the title street, the second part of which features characters like Schiller and Hoffman, and follows Lieutenant Pirogov's attempts to seduce a married woman.
This Russian author wrote "Nevsky Prospect." His other works include "The Overcoat," in which the ghost of Akaky Akakievich haunts St. Petersburg after his newly purchased suit is stolen.

Chichikov, the protagonist of this unfinished novel by Gogol, is theorized to be the one-legged Captain Kopeikin or Napoleon after it is revealed that he has been purchasing the deeds to deceased serfs.

bonuses.leadin: The first part of this work follows the life of Piskarev, who uses opium to treat his insomnia which he develops after following a beautiful woman to what turns out to be a brothel. For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Red River of the South forms much of the northern border between this state and Oklahoma. This state's cities include Lubbock and Amarillo.

In contrast to the Red River of the South, the Red River of the North forms this state's eastern border with Minnesota. It flows through this state's city of Grand Forks before emptying into Lake Winnipeg in Manitoba.

Meanwhile, another Red River has its mouth in this Asian country, where it flows into the Gulf of Tonkin. The river flows through this country's capital of Hanoi, and other cities in this country include Haiphong and Ho Chi Minh City.
acceptableAnswers: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about Red Rivers around the world, for 10 points each:

parts.text: This author wrote about the school Christminster, which is loosely based on Oxford, in his novel Jude the Obscure and he also penned Tess of the d'Urbervilles.

Hardy also penned this novel, which doesn't have much to do with Oxford. In it, Gabriel Oak eventually ends up with his beloved, Bathsheba Everdene, after a lot of farming and some rash actions by Mr. Boldwood.
acceptableAnswers: The Far From the Madding Crowd

parts.text: The Duke of Dorset's suicide by drowning himself in the River Isis triggers a rash of undergraduate suicides at Judas College, which is based on Oxford, in this author's novel Zuleika Dobson. He also wrote the collection Seven Men, which contains the story "Enoch Soames."

bonuses.leadin: Identify the following about fiction involving Oxford, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this Hindu temple complex, built in the 12th century in what is now Cambodia.

Scenes from the Ramayana and the Mahabharata as well as the Churning of the Sea of Milk are displayed at Angkor Wat in this sculptural style, in which sculpted characters have only small projection or depth away from the wall.
The Bayon temple at Angkor Wat demonstrates the influence of south Indian architecture through its eight examples of these monumental towers that can be found at the entrance of Hindu temples.

bonuses.leadin: This series of structures built by the Khmer people is the largest religious complex in the world. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this inefficient, often anaerobic method of energy production. Yeast cells use this process, consuming carbohydrates like sugar and creating byproducts like ethanol.

Instead of fermentation, aerobic organisms use the citric acid cycle to generate energy. One crucial step of the cycle is the production of citrate from water, oxaloacetate, and this carbon-containing molecule.
Production of Acetyl-CoA, and the rest of the citric acid cycle, occurs in the matrix of this organelle, the "powerhouse" of the eukaryotic cell.

bonuses.leadin: This process causes a buildup of lactic acid in exercising muscles. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Name this archetypal character, whose "journey" was analyzed in a work by Joseph Campbell.
acceptableAnswers: The Hero With A Thousand Faces

parts.text: Campbell's The Hero With A Thousand Faces is a foundational work in the field of comparative mythology, Other key works in comparative mythology include these two massive indexes intended to categorize folktales. Name either.

The first motif in Thompson's Motif-Index is about figures of this type, including one "from above." Sun gods or sky gods often fulfill this function, though some mythologies lack one of these figures entirely.

bonuses.leadin: According to one book, the "monomyth" begins with this character's "call to action" and ends with his return. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Give this name for the transition zone between the Sahara desert in the north and the savannah in the south.
This massive landlocked country named for the second-largest lake in Africa is the largest to occupy part of the Sahel. Its capital is N'Djamena.

The Aouzou strip controlled by Chad was believed to be rich in this resources, helping provoke a war with Libya. Australia has the world's largest known reserves of this resource, with 23% of the world supply.
